Without parallel investments in staffing and workflow redesign, compassion remains structurally precarious.

Limitations include the cross-sectional design, which precludes causal inference, and the single metropolitan setting, potentially limiting generalizability. Additionally, social desirability bias may have inflated nurse self-ratings.

---

Conclusion

This study proposes that compassionate nursing care be defined as an iterative relational process comprising five core elements: Attentive Presence, Emotional Responsiveness, Dignity Preservation, Advocacy, and Relational Continuity. Critically, these elements are not merely individual attributes but are contingent upon organizational conditions that protect nurses’ time and cognitive bandwidth. Operationalizing compassion through this empirically derived framework offers a pathway for clearer clinical education, valid quality metrics, and evidence-based staffing policy. Future research should test intervention bundles designed to enhance both the enactment and the perception of compassion, moving the discipline from abstract virtue to reproducible practice.

---

title: Expression profile and localization of vitellogenin mRNA and protein during ovarian development in turbot (Scophthalmus maximus)
text: Vitellogenin (Vtg) is the primary precursor of yolk proteins and is essential for oogenesis and embryonic development in oviparous teleosts. To elucidate the reproductive physiology of turbot (*Scophthalmus maximus*), this study characterized the expression profile and localization of vitellogenin mRNA and protein throughout ovarian development. Ovarian tissues were collected at distinct oogenic stages, including perinucleolus, cortical alveolus, vitellogenesis, and oocyte maturation. Temporal expression of *vtg* mRNA was quantified by real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR), while protein levels and spatial distribution were assessed by Western blotting and immunohistochemistry (IHC), respectively. The results showed that *vtg* mRNA levels remained low during early oogenesis, increased significantly upon vitellogenesis onset, peaked during the vitellogenic stage, and declined during maturation. Western blot analysis detected Vtg protein predominantly in vitellogenic ovaries. IHC staining revealed that Vtg initially appeared in the oocyte cytoplasm at early vitellogenesis and progressively accumulated within yolk granules as development advanced. Strong immunoreactivity was observed in the ooplasm of vitellogenic oocytes, whereas pre-vitellogenic and mature oocytes exhibited weak or negligible staining. Collectively, these findings demonstrate a stage-specific spatiotemporal pattern of Vtg synthesis and deposition during turbot ovarian development. This study provides molecular and histological evidence supporting the pivotal role of Vtg in vitellogenesis and advances our understanding of oogenic regulation in flatfish, with potential applications in broodstock management and aquaculture.

title: Strategies for narrowing the maize yield gap of household farms through precision fertigation under irrigated conditions using CERES-Maize model
text:
Strategies for narrowing the maize yield gap of household farms through precision fertigation under irrigated conditions using CERES-Maize model

Abstract

Yield gaps in maize production under irrigated conditions remain substantial for household farms due to suboptimal water and nutrient management. This study employed the CERES-Maize model within the DSSAT framework to quantify yield gaps and develop precision fertigation strategies for smallholder systems. Field experiments and model calibration were conducted across three consecutive growing seasons (2021–2023) in the North China Plain. Baseline farmer practice (FP), conventional uniform fertigation (UF), and four precision fertigation scenarios (PF1–PF4) with variable nitrogen (N) splits and irrigation scheduling were simulated. Results indicated a significant yield gap of 3.8 t ha⁻¹ (31%) between average farmer yields (8.5 t ha⁻¹) and attainable yields (12.3 t ha⁻¹). Precision fertigation scenarios PF3 and PF4, characterized by site-specific N application (180 kg N ha⁻¹) and deficit irrigation aligned with critical growth stages, achieved mean yields of 11.6–11.9 t ha⁻¹, effectively closing 85–92% of the yield gap. Compared to FP, the optimal strategy reduced water use by 24% and N surplus by 29%, while increasing net returns by 18%. These findings demonstrate that model-guided precision fertigation offers a robust pathway to narrow yield gaps sustainably in household farming systems.

Keywords: CERES-Maize; DSSAT; yield gap; precision fertigation; household farm; water use efficiency

1. Introduction

Global maize demand continues to escalate driven by food, feed, and bioenergy requirements. In intensive irrigated systems, particularly across the North China Plain (NCP), household farms dominate the agricultural landscape yet frequently exhibit significant yield gaps attributed to inefficient input management. Traditional flood irrigation combined with single basal fertilizer application leads to substantial water losses, nutrient leaching, and environmental degradation. Although irrigation infrastructure is available, temporal mismatches between crop demand and input supply persist among smallholders due to limited technical guidance.

Precision fertigation, integrating drip irrigation with soluble fertilizer application, presents a promising approach to synchronize water and nutrient supply with crop requirements. However, the adoption of such technology by household farms requires evidence-based prescriptions that account for local biophysical conditions and economic constraints. Process-based crop models, notably CERES-Maize embedded in the Decision Support System for Agrotechnology Transfer (DSSAT), offer mechanistic frameworks to evaluate management scenarios without extensive multi-year field trials. Despite previous applications of CERES-Maize in simulating maize responses to water and nitrogen, few studies have explicitly targeted yield gap closure through precision fertigation protocols tailored to household-scale irrigated systems.

Therefore, the objectives of this study were to: (i) quantify the maize yield gap between actual farmer practice and simulated attainable yield under irrigated conditions; (ii) design and evaluate precision fertigation scenarios using the CERES-Maize model; and (iii) identify economically viable and environmentally sustainable strategies suitable for household farms.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1. Study Area and Field Data

The study was conducted in Quzhou County (36.9°N, 115.2°E), Hebei Province, China, representing a typical double-cropping winter wheat–summer maize system on the NCP. Soil was a silt loam (Typic Haplustept) with bulk density of 1.45 g cm⁻³, field capacity of 0.32 cm³ cm⁻³, and wilting point of 0.13 cm³ cm⁻³. Weather data (daily maximum and minimum temperature, solar radiation, precipitation) were obtained from a local meteorological station. Three years (2021–2023) of field experiments provided phenological, biomass, grain yield, and soil moisture data for model calibration and validation. Cultivar Zhengdan 958, widely planted by local household farms, was used.

2.2. Model Calibration and Validation

The CERES-Maize model (version 4.8) in DSSAT v4.8 was parameterized for the local cultivar using genetic coefficients (P1, P2, P5, G2, G3, PHINT) derived from observed anthesis and physiological maturity dates, grain number, and grain-filling rates. Soil parameters, including saturated hydraulic conductivity and organic carbon content, were measured to 200 cm depth. The model was calibrated using 2021 data and validated against independent datasets from 2022 and 2023. Performance was assessed using the root mean square error (RMSE), normalized RMSE (NRMSE), and the index of agreement (d-index).

2.3. Scenario Design

Six management scenarios were simulated over a 30-year historical weather record (1994–2023) to account for climatic variability:

- FP (Farmer Practice): Flood irrigation (120 mm per event) at jointing and filling stages; basal N 180 kg ha⁻¹ as urea, no topdressing.
- UF (Uniform Fertigation): Drip irrigation with uniform N application (180 kg ha⁻¹) split 30% at V6, 40% at VT, and 30% at R1; irrigation triggered at 65% field capacity (FC).
- PF1: Reduced N (150 kg ha⁻¹) with same irrigation as UF.
- PF2: Standard N (180 kg ha⁻¹) with irrigation triggered at 55% FC.
- PF3: Variable-rate N (180 kg ha⁻¹) adjusted by growth stage demand—20% at V6, 50% at VT, 30% at R1—plus regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) with 80% ETc replenishment except full ETc at flowering.
- PF4: Optimized PF3 with 160 kg N ha⁻¹ and sensor-informed irrigation scheduling.

A control scenario with no water or N stress was included to define the attainable yield (Yw).

2.4. Data Analysis

Yield gap was calculated as Yw minus simulated actual yield for each scenario. Water use efficiency (WUE) was computed as grain yield divided by seasonal evapotranspiration (ET). Partial factor productivity of N (PFPN) and economic net returns (based on local input prices and maize grain price of $0.28 kg⁻¹) were analyzed.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1. Model Performance

CERES-Maize demonstrated satisfactory performance in simulating grain yield, anthesis, and maturity dates. Validation across 2022–2023 showed RMSE of 0.62 t ha⁻¹ and NRMSE of 5.8% for yield, with a d-index of 0.94. Phenological predictions were within 2–3 days of observed dates, confirming the model's reliability for scenario analysis.

3.2. Yield Gap Assessment

The 30-year average attainable yield (Yw) under fully irrigated and non-limiting N conditions was 12.3 t ha⁻¹. In contrast, simulated FP averaged 8.5 t ha⁻¹, revealing a consistent yield gap of 3.8 t ha⁻¹ (31%). Yield variability in FP was high (coefficient of variation, CV = 18%), driven by erratic rainfall and inefficient N uptake. UF improved mean yield to 10.1 t ha⁻¹, closing 42% of the gap but still leaving 2.2 t ha⁻¹ unexploited.

3.3. Precision Fertigation Scenarios

Precision scenarios substantially outperformed conventional practices. PF1 achieved 10.4 t ha⁻¹ with reduced N, indicating that better temporal distribution partially compensated for lower N input. PF2 reached 10.8 t ha⁻¹, demonstrating the benefit of tighter soil moisture thresholds. Notably, PF3 and PF4 achieved mean yields of 11.6 t ha⁻¹ and 11.9 t ha⁻¹, respectively, closing 85% and 92% of the yield gap. Under PF4, the yield advantage was most pronounced in drier years (2014, 2019), where yields exceeded FP by 4.1 t ha⁻¹.

3.4. Water and Nitrogen Use Efficiency

Seasonal irrigation water applied in FP totaled 360 mm, whereas PF3 and PF4 required 274 mm and 268 mm, representing 24% and 26% savings. Correspondingly, WUE increased from 1.72 kg m⁻³ in FP to 2.38 kg m⁻³ in PF4. Regarding N management, FP resulted in significant N surplus (68 kg N ha⁻¹) and low PFPN (47 kg grain kg⁻¹ N). PF4 reduced the N surplus to 21 kg ha⁻¹ and elevated PFPN to 74 kg grain kg⁻¹ N, mitigating leaching risk.

3.5. Economic Analysis

Despite higher operational costs associated with drip infrastructure, the optimized scenarios proved economically advantageous. Net returns for PF3 and PF4 averaged $2,840 and $2,910 ha⁻¹, respectively, compared with $2,420 ha⁻¹ for FP and $2,650 ha⁻¹ for UF. The benefit-cost ratio for PF4 reached 2.14, driven by yield gains and savings in water and fertilizer costs. Sensitivity analysis indicated that PF4 remained profitable provided maize prices exceeded $0.22 kg⁻¹.

4. Discussion

This study demonstrates that precision fertigation, guided by process-based modeling, can substantially narrow maize yield gaps in household irrigated systems. The 3.8 t ha⁻¹ yield gap identified here aligns with previous estimates for the NCP, yet our contribution lies in quantifying the specific contribution of synchronized water-N management. The superiority of PF3 and PF4 underscores the importance of matching N supply with crop demand curves rather than relying solely on irrigation refinement. The regulated deficit irrigation strategy during vegetative stages, combined with full ETc replenishment at flowering, appears critical for maximizing water productivity without yield penalty.

However, several limitations warrant consideration. First, the CERES-Maize model assumes homogeneous soil conditions, whereas household farms often exhibit high spatial variability at sub-field scales. Second, the economic analysis did not fully amortize the capital cost of drip systems over their lifespan; inclusion of subsidy schemes common in China would further improve profitability. Third, farmer adoption depends on technical literacy and labor availability, factors not captured in biophysical modeling. Future research should integrate remote sensing data for real-time fertigation adjustments and explore the scalability of these strategies across diverse smallholder typologies.

5. Conclusion

Using the CERES-Maize model, this study quantified a 31% yield gap in household farm maize production under irrigated conditions and demonstrated that precision fertigation strategies can close up to 92% of this gap. The optimal strategy, integrating stage-specific N splits with regulated deficit irrigation, achieved 11.9 t ha⁻¹ while reducing water use by 26% and N surplus by 29%. These results provide a robust, evidence-based framework for promoting sustainable intensification on household farms. Widespread adoption of model-informed precision fertigation could simultaneously enhance food security, resource efficiency, and farmer profitability in intensive irrigated maize systems.

title: Knowledge, attitude, and practice of medication among Haikou residents
text:
Medication-related problems remain a significant global public health concern, contributing substantially to preventable morbidity, mortality, and escalating healthcare expenditures. The World Health Organization has long emphasized rational use of medicines as a cornerstone of health system performance, which fundamentally depends on informed public participation. Patients' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding medication serve as critical determinants of therapeutic outcomes, influencing adherence patterns, self-care behaviors, and the likelihood of adverse drug events. Inadequate pharmacological literacy—particularly concerning drug indications, proper dosages, storage conditions, and potential adverse effects—frequently culminates in medication errors, antimicrobial resistance, and unnecessary hospitalizations, posing severe challenges across diverse healthcare settings.

China has experienced unprecedented growth in pharmaceutical consumption driven by an aging society and expanded health insurance coverage. Nevertheless, accumulating evidence indicates that medication literacy among the general population remains insufficient, with marked regional disparities observed across diverse socioeconomic contexts. While medication KAP surveys have been undertaken in multiple mainland cities, comparable data from Haikou, the capital of Hainan Province and a strategic hub of the Hainan Free Trade Port, are notably absent. The city's distinctive tropical environment, rapidly aging demographic structure, and evolving healthcare demands associated with tourism and migration may engender unique medication use patterns that warrant specific investigation.

The present study was designed to comprehensively assess the knowledge, attitude, and practice of medication among Haikou residents. By quantifying current literacy levels, identifying prevalent misconceptions, and characterizing self-medication behaviors, we intend to furnish actionable insights for developing tailored health education strategies and informing local pharmaceutical policies to foster rational drug utilization.

title: Policy distortions, farm size, and the overuse of agricultural chemicals in China
text:
Results and Discussion

Table 2 presents the baseline OLS and instrumental-variable estimates. We document a pronounced inverse relationship between farm size and chemical input intensity: each additional hectare of operational scale reduces fertilizer expenditure per mu by 32.6 yuan (*p* < 0.01) and pesticide use by 0.48 kg/mu (*p* < 0.05). Households cultivating fewer than 0.67 hectares—the sample median—overapply nitrogen by 38% relative to county-level agronomic recommendations, whereas farms exceeding 2 hectares exceed the optimum by only 11%.

We identify policy distortions as the central mechanism amplifying this divergence. The interaction term between the land fragmentation index and subsidy dependence is positively associated with chemical intensity (coefficient = 0.193, *p* < 0.01), indicating that direct grain subsidies disproportionately incentivize input-intensive practices on small, scattered plots. Moreover, minimum grain price supports reduce the own-price elasticity of fertilizer demand by 0.15 for households operating under 1 hectare, effectively lowering the marginal cost of overapplication for smallholders.

These findings suggest that meeting China’s 2025 chemical reduction targets requires more than improved technical guidance. Without tenure reforms that lower transaction costs for land consolidation and a decoupling of area-based subsidies from input-intensive production, the structural penalties of small-scale farming will continue to drive excessive chemical use.

title: Factors influencing the quality of preconception healthcare in China: applying a preconceptional instrument to assess healthcare needs
text:
Factors influencing the quality of preconception healthcare in China: applying a preconceptional instrument to assess healthcare needs

Abstract

Preconception healthcare (PCH) is essential for reducing adverse pregnancy outcomes and promoting maternal–fetal health. Despite the nationwide expansion of free preconception check-up programmes in China, significant disparities in service quality and uptake persist. This study aimed to identify key factors influencing the quality of PCH and to assess healthcare needs using a standardized preconceptional instrument. A multicentre cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to June 2023 among 612 women of reproductive age across six maternal and child health hospitals in eastern, central, and western China. A validated 28-item Preconception Healthcare Needs Assessment Instrument (PHNAI), scored on a 0–100 scale, was used to measure PCH quality across four domains: knowledge, attitudes and practices, service accessibility, and psychological readiness. Multivariate linear regression and descriptive statistics were applied for data analysis. The mean PHNAI score was 68.4 (SD 12.3). Higher education level (β = 4.52, *p* < 0.001), urban residence (β = 3.89, *p* < 0.001), history of previous pregnancy (β = 2.76, *p* = 0.004), and participation in the National Free Preconception Health Examination Project (β = 5.14, *p* < 0.001) were independently associated with higher PCH quality. Conversely, unemployment (β = −3.45, *p* = 0.011) and lack of basic medical insurance (β = −2.98, *p* = 0.009) were significant negative predictors. These findings indicate that socioeconomic inequalities remain major barriers to high-quality PCH. Policy efforts should prioritize health-system strengthening for vulnerable populations and integrate needs-based assessments into routine preconception counselling.

Keywords: Preconception healthcare; Quality of care; Health needs assessment; China; Reproductive health

1. Introduction

Preconception healthcare (PCH) encompasses biomedical, behavioural, and social interventions provided to couples before conception to improve pregnancy outcomes and long-term child health. Over the past decade, China has made substantial progress in expanding PCH coverage through the National Free Preconception Health Examination Project (NFPCP), which offers counselling, risk assessment, and medical examinations to millions of couples annually. However, emerging evidence suggests that high coverage does not necessarily equate to high quality. Variations in service accessibility, counselling depth, and continuity of care continue to undermine the effectiveness of PCH, particularly among rural, low-income, and migrant populations.

Existing literature has extensively documented the prevalence of preconception risk factors—such as folic acid deficiency, chronic diseases, and advanced maternal age—but few studies have employed standardized instruments to quantify healthcare needs from the user’s perspective or to evaluate the multifactorial determinants of PCH quality. Without precise measurement tools, health providers and policymakers lack actionable data to tailor interventions. To address this gap, the present study applies a newly developed preconceptional instrument to assess healthcare needs and investigates the demographic, socioeconomic, and health-system factors that influence the quality of PCH in China. The findings are expected to inform targeted strategies for improving equitable delivery of preconception services.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1. Study design and setting

A multicentre cross-sectional study was conducted between March and June 2023 in six maternal and child health (MCH) hospitals located in two provinces each from the eastern, central, and western regions of China. These sites were purposively selected to capture geographic and economic diversity.

2.2. Participants and sampling

Women aged 20–40 years who were planning pregnancy within the next 12 months were eligible for inclusion. Exclusion criteria included known infertility diagnoses, severe psychiatric disorders, and non-Chinese speakers. A consecutive sampling strategy was used at outpatient preconception clinics. A total of 680 women were approached, of whom 612 completed the questionnaire (response rate 90.0%). The study was approved by the institutional ethics committee, and all participants provided written informed consent.

2.3. Instruments and measurements

The primary instrument was the Preconception Healthcare Needs Assessment Instrument (PHNAI), a 28-item tool developed and validated for the Chinese context. It comprises four domains: (1) preconception knowledge (9 items); (2) attitudes and health practices (8 items); (3) service accessibility and system navigation (7 items); and (4) psychological readiness and social support (4 items). Responses were recorded on a 5-point Likert scale and linearly transformed to a 0–100 scale, with higher scores indicating better PCH quality or greater unmet needs depending on the domain. In this analysis, the aggregate score was used as a proxy for overall PCH quality. The instrument demonstrated good internal consistency in this sample (Cronbach’s α = 0.84).

Sociodemographic variables included age, educational attainment, household income, employment status, medical insurance type, place of residence (urban/rural), parity history, and prior participation in the NFPCP.

2.4. Statistical analysis

Data were analysed using SPSS version 26.0. Continuous variables were presented as means with standard deviations (SD), and categorical variables as frequencies with percentages. Group differences in PHNAI scores were examined using independent-sample *t*-tests and one-way ANOVA. Multivariate linear regression was performed to identify independent factors associated with PCH quality, adjusting for age and region. Statistical significance was set at *p* < 0.05.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1. Participant characteristics

The mean age of participants was 28.5 years (SD 3.4). Approximately 45.4% held a bachelor’s degree or higher, 51.8% resided in urban areas, and 62.1% were nulliparous. Roughly 58.0% reported monthly household incomes between 5,000 and 15,000 RMB. A total of 67.3% had participated in the NFPCP, whereas 18.6% were uninsured or lacked basic medical insurance coverage.

3.2. Preconception healthcare quality scores

The overall mean PHNAI score was 68.4 (SD 12.3) out of 100. Domain-specific scores revealed that knowledge was relatively high (mean 72.1, SD 14.5), whereas service accessibility scored lowest (mean 61.3, SD 15.2), followed by attitudes and practices (mean 66.8, SD 13.1) and psychological readiness (mean 70.5, SD 12.8). Notably, 62.4% of participants expressed a strong need for genetic counselling, 58.0% requested structured nutritional guidance, and 45.1% identified out-of-pocket costs as a barrier to obtaining recommended preconception tests.

3.3. Factors associated with PCH quality

Univariate analyses showed significant associations between PHNAI scores and education level (*p* < 0.001), residence (*p* < 0.001), household income (*p* = 0.002), employment status (*p* = 0.008), medical insurance status (*p* = 0.008), parity (*p* = 0.015), and NFPCP participation (*p* < 0.001). Age and marital duration were not significantly associated with overall scores.

In the multivariate linear regression model, higher education emerged as the strongest sociodemographic predictor (β = 4.52, 95% CI: 2.91–6.13, *p* < 0.001). Urban residence was also positively associated with PCH quality (β = 3.89, 95% CI: 2.18–5.60, *p* < 0.001). Women with a history of previous pregnancy scored 2.76 points higher than nulliparous women (95% CI: 0.88–4.64, *p* = 0.004), suggesting that prior maternity experience facilitates engagement with preconception services. Participation in the NFPCP was associated with a 5.14-point increase in quality scores (95% CI: 3.42–6.86, *p* < 0.001).

Conversely, unemployment was negatively associated with PCH quality (β = −3.45, 95% CI: −6.09 to −0.81, *p* = 0.011), as was the absence of basic medical insurance (β = −2.98, 95% CI: −5.18 to −0.78, *p* = 0.009). These results suggest that economic vulnerability and inadequate risk protection substantially compromise preconception care experiences.

4. Discussion

This study demonstrates that the quality of preconception healthcare in China is significantly stratified by socioeconomic status, geographic residence, and health-system engagement. The mean PHNAI score of 68.4 indicates considerable room for improvement, particularly in the domain of service accessibility, which recorded the lowest performance. This finding underscores a critical implementation gap: while knowledge levels among Chinese women appear adequate, translating awareness into accessible, affordable, and continuous care remains challenging.

The positive association between higher education and PCH quality aligns with established health literacy frameworks, whereby educated individuals are more likely to seek information, navigate health systems effectively, and adhere to preconception recommendations. Similarly, the urban advantage likely reflects the concentration of specialized MCH resources, transportation convenience, and shorter wait times in metropolitan areas. The protective effect of prior pregnancy may stem from increased familiarity with maternity services and heightened motivation to avoid recurrent complications.

The strongest modifiable predictor identified was participation in the NFPCP, which was associated with a clinically meaningful increase in PHNAI scores. This supports the continued expansion of government-subsidized preconception programmes. Nevertheless, the negative influence of unemployment and lack of insurance signals that population-wide coverage does not automatically reach the most vulnerable groups. Informal workers, rural migrants, and uninsured women may face hidden costs, lost wages, or geographic barriers that discourage utilization.

Several limitations should be acknowledged. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inferences. Additionally, the sample was restricted to women attending MCH hospitals, potentially excluding couples who never enter the formal health system. Future research should adopt longitudinal designs and incorporate male partners to capture couple-level dynamics.

5. Conclusion

The quality of preconception healthcare in China is influenced by a complex interplay of educational attainment, residential location, employment security, insurance coverage, and programme participation. The PHNAI offers a practical, validated approach to identifying population-specific needs and system deficiencies. To advance equitable PCH, policymakers should integrate needs-based assessments into primary care, expand insurance reimbursement for preconception interventions beyond basic screening, and deploy targeted outreach for rural, unemployed, and low-literacy populations. Closing these gaps will be essential for maximizing the population health returns of China’s preconception care investments.

title: Cognition of agriculture waste and payments for a circular agriculture model in Central China
text:
The inefficient utilization and improper disposal of agricultural waste (AW) pose significant environmental challenges and constrain sustainable agricultural development in Central China. Transitioning toward a circular agriculture model (CAM) presents a viable pathway for waste valorization and ecological conservation; however, successful implementation hinges upon stakeholders' cognitive engagement and adequate financial mechanisms. Despite growing attention to AW recycling technologies, limited empirical research has simultaneously examined farmers' cognitive constructs regarding waste reuse and their willingness to pay (WTP) for CAM adoption within this specific agro-ecological region.

This study investigates rural households' cognition of agricultural waste and their payment preferences for supporting a circular agricultural system across Central China. Drawing on household survey data collected from respondents in major agricultural provinces during recent production cycles, we employed a structural equation model to dissect the determinants of waste cognition and utilized the contingent valuation method to estimate payment intentions. 

Results indicate that while farmers demonstrate heightened environmental awareness of AW pollution, their cognitive understanding of CAM's long-term economic benefits remains inadequate. Perceived behavioral control, environmental responsibility, and government policy trust significantly enhance CAM adoption intentions and WTP. Conversely, income constraints, risk aversion, and insufficient technical extension services negatively moderate the cognition-payment nexus. Substantial heterogeneity in WTP was observed across farm scales, waste types, and prior participation in eco-compensation programs. 

These findings underscore that fostering cognitive transitions through targeted educational interventions and establishing differentiated payment-for-ecosystem-services schemes are imperative. Policy recommendations include integrating cognitive-behavioral incentives with financial subsidies, developing regional AW recycling infrastructure, and tailoring compensation standards to local farming contexts to facilitate the widespread adoption of circular agriculture in Central China.

title: Key mechanisms of micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) toxicity across taxonomic groups
text:
Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are recognized as pervasive anthropogenic pollutants threatening biodiversity across aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Despite extensive evidence of adverse effects, whether core toxicity mechanisms are phylogenetically conserved or taxon-specific remains unresolved. We conducted a standardized comparative assessment using four phylogenetically distinct species: the green alga *Chlorella vulgaris*, the cladoceran *Daphnia magna*, the zebrafish *Danio rerio*, and the earthworm *Eisenia fetida*. Organisms were exposed to spherical polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs, 0.1–10 μm) and nanoplastics (PS-NPs, 50 nm) at environmentally relevant concentrations. Endpoints included reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, lipid peroxidation, antioxidant enzyme activities, mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), gene expression, reproductive output, and histopathology. Nanoplastics consistently elicited stronger toxicity than microplastics across all taxa. Algae exhibited photosystem II inhibition, with Fv/Fm reduced by 42% at 5 mg/L NPs. *Daphnia* showed the highest reproductive sensitivity, displaying a 58% fecundity decline at 1 mg/L NPs. Zebrafish larvae manifested p53/caspase-3-mediated apoptosis, mitochondrial depolarization, and neurotoxicity (35% acetylcholinesterase inhibition). Earthworms suffered intestinal barrier disruption and reduced cocoon production. We propose that oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and epithelial barrier damage represent conserved core mechanisms, whereas photosynthetic disruption and neurotoxicity are taxon-specific. These findings establish a mechanistic foundation for cross-taxa ecological risk assessment of MNPs.

Keywords: Microplastics; Nanoplastics; Cross-taxa toxicity; Oxidative stress; Mitochondrial dysfunction; Ecological risk assessment

1. Introduction

Microplastics (<5 mm) and nanoplastics (<1 μm) have emerged as contaminants of concern in virtually all ecosystems, from marine abysses to agricultural topsoils. Originating from the environmental weathering of larger debris or direct release from consumer products, MNPs are readily internalized by organisms across trophic levels, triggering sublethal and lethal outcomes. While mechanistic studies have proliferated, most focus on single species using diverse polymer types, particle morphologies, and exposure regimens that preclude direct cross-taxa comparison. Consequently, a coherent understanding of whether fundamental toxicity pathways are universally conserved or predominantly lineage-specific remains elusive.

This knowledge gap carries significant ecological and regulatory implications. Photosynthetic producers may primarily suffer from surface shading and membrane-bound oxidative bursts, whereas filter-feeding zooplankton face physical ingestion and gut obstruction. Vertebrates, possessing complex immune and neuroendocrine systems, may additionally experience inflammatory and neurotoxic perturbations. Soil invertebrates encounter distinct exposure routes via dermal contact and sediment ingestion. Elucidating how these taxonomic groups converge or diverge in their mechanistic responses is critical for constructing predictive species-sensitivity distributions and robust environmental quality standards.

The influence of particle size adds further complexity. Nanoplastics possess a higher surface-area-to-volume ratio and enhanced bioavailability, potentially enabling translocation across cellular membranes and access to organelles such as mitochondria. Yet, cross-taxa evaluations that systematically isolate the role of particle dimensions while holding polymer chemistry constant remain scarce. Therefore, the present study was designed to compare PS-MPs and PS-NPs across four representative species: the primary producer *C. vulgaris*, the primary consumer *D. magna*, the vertebrate *D. rerio*, and the soil detritivore *E. fetida*. By standardizing polymer type, shape, and endpoint batteries, we aimed to (i) quantify comparative sensitivities, (ii) distinguish conserved from taxon-specific molecular mechanisms, and (iii) evaluate the influence of particle size on toxicity across distinct biological organizational levels.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1. MNP Preparation and Characterization
Spherical polystyrene microplastics (0.1–10 μm) and nanoplastics (50 nm) were obtained as aqueous suspensions and characterized by dynamic light scattering (DLS) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Stock suspensions were sonicated (40 kHz, 15 min) prior to dilution. Nominal exposure concentrations ranged from 1 to 100 mg/L for MPs and 0.1 to 10 mg/L for NPs, bracketing environmentally reported values. Vehicle controls contained 0.001% Tween-80; no significant differences were observed between vehicle and negative controls (p > 0.05).

2.2. Test Organisms and Exposure Protocols
*Chlorella vulgaris* was cultured in OECD TG 201 medium. Cells (2 × 10⁴ cells/mL) were exposed to MNPs for 96 h under continuous illumination. Growth inhibition, chlorophyll-a content, and maximum quantum yield of photosystem II (Fv/Fm) were quantified.

*Daphnia magna* neonates (<24 h) were maintained in ISO standard medium. A 21-day chronic reproduction test followed OECD TG 211, with daily renewal of MNP suspensions. Mortality, body length, and cumulative fecundity were recorded.

Zebrafish (*Danio rerio*) embryos (2 h post-fertilization) were exposed in 24-well plates for 7 days. At 7 days post-fertilization, larvae were sampled for biochemical assays: ROS, malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity. Gene expression of *p53*, *caspase-3*, and *il1b* was quantified by quantitative PCR.

*Eisenia fetida* adults were exposed in artificial soil (OECD TG 207) spiked with MNPs for 14 days. Coelomocyte viability was measured via MTT assay. Gut tissue was processed for histopathological examination (H&E staining). Cocoon production was monitored weekly.

2.3. Statistical Analyses
Each treatment included five replicates, and experiments were performed twice independently. Data are presented as mean ± standard deviation (SD). Differences between control and treatment groups were determined using one-way ANOVA followed by Dunnett’s post-hoc test (p < 0.05). EC₅₀ values were calculated by probit analysis.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1. Comparative Sensitivity and Size-Dependent Toxicity
Nanoplastics induced markedly more severe effects than microplastics across all taxa. In *C. vulgaris*, the 96-h EC₅₀ for growth inhibition was 8.2 mg/L for NPs compared with 35.6 mg/L for MPs. At the highest MP concentration (100 mg/L), algal growth was inhibited by only 22%, whereas 5 mg/L NPs reduced Fv/Fm by 42% and chlorophyll-a content by 33%, indicating substantial photosystem II impairment.

*D. magna* exhibited extreme sensitivity to reproductive toxicity. The 21-day LOEC for fecundity was 1 mg/L for NPs and 10 mg/L for MPs. At 1 mg/L NPs, cumulative offspring per female decreased from 124 ± 11 in controls to 52 ± 8, a 58% reduction (p < 0.001). By contrast, 10 mg/L MPs caused only a modest 15% fecundity decline. Maternal body length was significantly reduced at ≥5 mg/L NPs.

In zebrafish larvae, exposure to 1 mg/L NPs significantly elevated ROS levels by 2.8-fold and MDA by 2.1-fold relative to controls (p < 0.01). Antioxidant enzymes exhibited a non-monotonic response: SOD and CAT activities increased at 1 mg/L but declined precipitously at 10 mg/L, suggesting antioxidant depletion. MMP decreased by 45% at 5 mg/L NPs, indicative of mitochondrial depolarization. Transcript levels of *p53*, *caspase-3*, and *il1b* were upregulated 3.2-, 2.7-, and 4.1-fold, respectively, at 5 mg/L NPs (all p < 0.01). Concurrently, AChE activity decreased by 35%, pointing to neurotoxic potential.

*E. fetida* exposed to 5 mg/L NPs showed a 40% reduction in coelomocyte viability. Histopathology revealed disintegration of the intestinal epithelium, microvilli loss, and accumulation of nanoplastic aggregates in the coelomic cavity. Cocoon production dropped from 8.2 ± 1.1 per individual in controls to 3.1 ± 0.9 at 5 mg/L NPs over 14 days.

3.2. Conserved vs. Taxon-Specific Mechanisms
Oxidative stress, evidenced by elevated ROS and lipid peroxidation, represented the most conserved mechanism across all four species. Mitochondrial impairment, manifested as MMP loss, was observed in the three animal species, linking oxidative imbalance to cellular energy crisis. Upregulation of pro-apoptotic and inflammatory genes in zebrafish, coupled with coelomocyte mortality and gut damage in earthworms, suggests that barrier dysfunction and programmed cell death are shared downstream consequences.

Conversely, photosynthetic inhibition was unique to algae, driven by surface shading and chloroplast membrane damage. Neurotoxicity, manifested as AChE inhibition in zebrafish, was specific to the vertebrate model. Physical entanglement and gut blockage were prominent in *Daphnia* and earthworms, but internal translocation of NPs across biological barriers was size-dependent and most pronounced in fish larvae and worm coelomocytes.

4. Discussion

Our comparative analysis reveals that while the magnitude of MNP toxicity varies among phylogenetically distant organisms, a core suite of mechanistic pathways—principally oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and epithelial barrier disruption—is phylogenetically conserved. This conservation likely stems from the fundamental role of redox homeostasis and membrane integrity in all eukaryotic cells. The smaller size of NPs endowed them with a greater capacity to cross cellular membranes, localize to mitochondria, and trigger intracellular ROS bursts, explaining their universally higher potency relative to MPs.

The pronounced reproductive sensitivity of *D. magna* aligns with its filter-feeding ecology and continuous exposure via ingestion. The 58% fecundity decline at environmentally plausible NP concentrations underscores the vulnerability of primary consumers and raises concerns for food-web stability. In contrast, the algal response was characterized by photosystem II photoinhibition, a mechanism irrelevant to heterotrophic animals but ecologically significant because it can constrain basal productivity and propagate upward

title: Inpatient Dignity Scale: Mandarin translation and psychometric characteristics evaluation
text:
Patient dignity constitutes a cornerstone of ethical healthcare delivery and profoundly influences patients' psychological well-being, treatment adherence, and overall satisfaction during hospitalization. For hospitalized individuals, the experience of dignity is particularly salient, as acute illness, loss of autonomy, and exposure to the potentially dehumanizing aspects of medical care may render patients exceptionally vulnerable. Although dignity has gained increasing attention as a measurable quality indicator in global health discourse, its systematic assessment in inpatient settings remains limited, particularly in non-Western contexts where linguistically and culturally appropriate instruments are scarce.

The Inpatient Dignity Scale (IDS) was developed as a self-report instrument to capture multidimensional aspects of dignity specifically among hospitalized adults, encompassing critical domains such as sense of self-worth, interpersonal respect, environmental privacy, and autonomy preservation. While the original English version and several translated adaptations have demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity across diverse healthcare systems, no Mandarin Chinese version has been established to date. This absence is particularly consequential given China's immense hospital-based population and distinct sociocultural conceptualizations of dignity, face, and interpersonal harmony, which may shape patients' experiences and expressions of dignified care in ways that differ meaningfully from Western individualistic frameworks.

Therefore, the present study was designed to translate the IDS into Mandarin Chinese following rigorous forward-backward translation and expert panel cross-cultural adaptation protocols, and to comprehensively evaluate its psychometric properties among Chinese-speaking inpatients. Specifically, we examined internal consistency, test-retest reliability, content validity, and construct validity through both classical test theory approaches and confirmatory factor analysis. By establishing a psychometrically robust and culturally resonant Mandarin version of the IDS, this research aims to provide Chinese clinicians and health services researchers with a validated instrument to identify dignity-related deficits, evaluate humanistic care initiatives, and facilitate meaningful cross-cultural comparisons in inpatient dignity research.

title: Better understanding of homologous recombination through a 12-week laboratory course for undergraduates majoring in biotechnology
text: Of the 34 enrolled students, 82% scored below 60% on the pre-course assessment of homologous recombination (HR) mechanisms. Post-course, mean scores increased from 52% to 84% (*p* < 0.001), and 91% correctly diagrammed the double-strand break repair pathway. In practical sessions, 76% of students successfully generated a knockout construct by week 10, with 68% confirming integration via PCR. Student confidence surveys showed a rise from 2.3 to 4.1 on a 5-point Likert scale. These gains suggest that iterative experimental design—particularly troubleshooting failed transformation attempts—solidified theoretical knowledge more effectively than lecture alone. However, 24% of construct failures were linked to primer design errors, indicating that bioinformatics modules require strengthening. Overall, the 12-week format provided sufficient time to link molecular theory with technical execution, significantly enhancing HR comprehension and laboratory autonomy among biotechnology undergraduates.

title: An empirical research on evaluating banks' credit assessment of corporate customers
text:
An empirical research on evaluating banks' credit assessment of corporate customers

Abstract

This study empirically evaluates the effectiveness of credit assessment models employed by commercial banks for corporate customers. Using a proprietary dataset of 512 manufacturing firms that obtained loans from a major commercial bank between 2019 and 2023, we compare the predictive performance of a traditional logistic regression model against a machine learning random forest approach. The analysis incorporates financial ratios, qualitative firm-specific indicators, and macroeconomic variables. Our results reveal that the cash flow coverage ratio, debt-to-asset ratio, and industry risk index are the most significant predictors of corporate default. The random forest model achieves an AUC of 0.89, outperforming the logistic regression model (AUC = 0.82). We find that integrating non-financial and macroeconomic factors into credit scoring systems substantially enhances banks' risk identification capabilities. These findings offer practical implications for refining internal rating-based systems and regulatory stress-testing frameworks.

Keywords: Credit risk assessment; Corporate default prediction; Logistic regression; Random forest; Financial ratios

1. Introduction

Effective credit risk assessment remains a cornerstone of commercial banking and financial stability. Under the Basel III and forthcoming Basel IV frameworks, banks are required to maintain robust internal rating systems to estimate probability of default (PD) and mitigate unexpected losses. However, traditional credit evaluation models often rely heavily on historical financial statements and collateral value, which may suffer from information asymmetry and timeliness issues, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). In recent years, the proliferation of machine learning (ML) techniques has offered alternative approaches to credit scoring, yet their adoption in prudential banking practice remains limited due to interpretability concerns and regulatory constraints.

This study aims to empirically evaluate and compare the predictive validity of conventional statistical methods and ML algorithms in the context of banks' credit assessment of corporate customers. Specifically, we seek to (1) identify the key financial and non-financial determinants of corporate default in a major commercial bank’s loan portfolio, (2) compare the classification performance of logistic regression and random forest models, and (3) discuss the trade-offs between predictive accuracy and model interpretability for regulatory compliance. By using a unique dataset comprising 512 corporate borrowers from the manufacturing sector, this research contributes to the ongoing discourse on augmenting traditional credit risk models with qualitative and macroeconomic variables.

2. Materials and Methods

Our sample consists of 512 manufacturing firms that received term loans from a large commercial bank in China between January 2019 and December 2023. Among these borrowers, 58 firms (11.3%) experienced default events, defined as overdue payments exceeding 90 days within 12 months after loan disbursement. Data were collected from the bank’s internal credit database, supplemented by Wind and CSMAR financial repositories.

The dependent variable is a binary default indicator (1 = default, 0 = non-default). Independent variables are categorized into three groups. Financial indicators include the debt-to-asset ratio (DAR), current ratio (CR), return on assets (ROA), operating cash flow coverage ratio (OCFCR), and revenue growth rate (REVGR). Non-financial indicators encompass firm age (AGE), a state-owned enterprise dummy (SOE), an industry risk score (IRS) compiled by the bank’s risk management department, and credit history length (CHL). Macroeconomic controls include regional GDP growth (GDPGR) and the purchasing managers’ index (PMI).

We employ two modeling techniques. First, a binary logistic regression is used to estimate the linear relationship between explanatory variables and the log-odds of default: ln[P/(1−P)] = β₀ + ΣβᵢXᵢ + ε, where P denotes the probability of default. Variance inflation factors (VIF) are calculated to rule out multicollinearity; all VIF values are below 3.5. Second, a random forest (RF) classifier with 500 decision trees is trained to capture non-linear interactions and variable importance. The dataset is split into 80% training and 20% testing subsets. Model performance is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC). A five-fold cross-validation is conducted to ensure robustness.

3. Results and Analysis

Descriptive statistics indicate notable differences between defaulters and non-defaulters. Defaulting firms exhibit significantly lower cash flow coverage (mean OCFCR = 1.18 versus 2.84 for non-defaulters) and higher leverage (mean DAR = 72.4% versus 54.6%). They are also younger (mean AGE = 5.2 years versus 8.7 years) and tend to operate in industries with higher risk scores.

The logistic regression results show that OCFCR (β = −2.14, p < 0.01) and DAR (β = 3.21, p < 0.01) are the strongest predictors of default. The industry risk score is also statistically significant (β = 1.85, p < 0.05), whereas ROA and REVGR do not achieve conventional significance levels. The macroeconomic variables show modest explanatory power.

The random forest model identifies OCFCR, DAR, and IRS as the top three features by importance, collectively accounting for 57% of predictive power. Notably, the RF model uncovers a significant interaction between DAR and firm age, suggesting that high leverage is more dangerous for younger firms—a non-linear effect not fully captured by logistic regression.

In terms of out-of-sample performance, the RF model attains an accuracy of 87.3%, precision of 78.4%, recall of 81.0%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.89. The logistic model achieves 81.4% accuracy, 71.2% precision, 74.1% recall, and an AUC of 0.82. The five-fold cross-validation confirms the stability of these results, with standard deviations below 0.03.

4. Discussion

Our empirical findings corroborate the view that cash flow adequacy and capital structure are fundamental to corporate creditworthiness, consistent with the extant literature on financial distress prediction. The significance of the industry risk index underscores the necessity of incorporating sector-specific dynamics into bank-internal rating systems rather than relying solely on borrower-specific financials. The superior performance of the random forest model aligns with recent fintech studies, demonstrating that ML algorithms can effectively model complex, non-linear relationships in credit risk data.

Nevertheless, the trade-off between accuracy and interpretability warrants careful consideration. While the random forest improves predictive power by approximately seven percentage points in AUC, its "black box" nature poses challenges for regulatory compliance under Basel and IFRS 9 requirements, where banks must provide transparent and auditable justifications for credit decisions. Therefore, we advocate for a hybrid framework in which ML models serve as early warning screening tools, while logistic regression or structural models remain the basis for final provisioning and capital allocation.

This study is subject to limitations. The sample is drawn from a single bank and confined to the manufacturing sector, potentially limiting generalizability. Additionally, the sample size of 512 firms, though sufficient for preliminary inference, may constrain the training of more complex deep-learning architectures. Future research could expand the cross-sector sample and incorporate alternative data sources, such as supply-chain networks and textual sentiment from corporate disclosures.

5. Conclusion

This paper provides an empirical evaluation of banks' credit assessment of corporate customers by comparing traditional logistic regression with random forest machine learning. Our analysis of 512 manufacturing firms reveals that cash flow coverage, debt-to-asset ratio, and industry risk are the most influential predictors of default. The random forest model demonstrates superior classification performance, yet its opacity suggests that banks should adopt hybrid architectures balancing predictive accuracy with regulatory interpretability. These results offer actionable insights for refining internal credit rating systems and enhancing the precision of stress-testing exercises. Future studies may further benefit from integrating alternative big-data metrics to capture real-time corporate risk dynamics.

title: Exercise interventions for post-stroke depression: A protocol for systematic review and meta-analysis
text:
Exercise interventions for post-stroke depression: A protocol for systematic review and meta-analysis

Abstract

Background: Post-stroke depression (PSD) affects approximately one-third of survivors and impedes functional recovery. Exercise may alleviate depressive symptoms, yet existing evidence remains fragmented. Objective: To present a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating the efficacy and safety of exercise interventions for PSD. Methods: We will search PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and PsycINFO from inception to March 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing exercise with control in adults with PSD. Primary outcomes include depression severity (HAM-D or PHQ-9); secondary outcomes comprise quality of life and adverse events. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data, and assess risk of bias using RoB 2. We will perform random-effects meta-analyses and assess certainty with GRADE. Results: A pilot search retrieved 1,247 records, with approximately 12 RCTs anticipated for inclusion. Conclusion: This protocol provides a rigorous framework to synthesize evidence on exercise for PSD, informing clinical guidelines and rehabilitation practice.

Keywords: post-stroke depression; exercise; systematic review; meta-analysis; protocol; rehabilitation; randomized controlled trial

Introduction

Post-stroke depression (PSD) occurs in up to 33% of survivors and is associated with poorer functional outcomes, increased mortality, and reduced quality of life. Despite the availability of pharmacotherapy, antidepressants confer side effects and variable adherence in stroke populations. Emerging evidence suggests that structured exercise—including aerobic, resistance, and mind-body modalities—may modulate neuroplasticity and reduce inflammation, thereby alleviating depressive symptoms. However, current literature consists of heterogeneous trials with inconsistent reporting, precluding definitive conclusions. This protocol describes a systematic review and meta-analysis designed to rigorously evaluate the efficacy and safety of exercise interventions for adults with PSD, with the aim of informing evidence-based rehabilitation strategies.

Materials and Methods

This protocol was developed in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) 2015 statement and is registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025XXXXX).

Eligibility criteria: We will include peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluate structured exercise interventions (aerobic, resistance, mixed, or mind-body) versus usual care, waitlist, or sham exercise in adults (≥18 years) diagnosed with depression following stroke. We will exclude studies enrolling participants with major psychiatric comorbidities or active substance use disorders.

Information sources and search strategy: A comprehensive search will be conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and PsycINFO from database inception to March 15, 2025. The strategy will combine controlled vocabulary and free-text terms related to "stroke," "depression," and "exercise" without language restrictions. Reference lists of included studies and relevant reviews will be hand-searched.

Study selection and data extraction: Two independent reviewers will screen titles/abstracts and full texts using Rayyan QCRI. Disagreements will be resolved by consensus or a third reviewer. A standardized form will extract data on study characteristics, participant demographics, intervention parameters (frequency, intensity, type, duration), comparator details, and outcome measures.

Risk of bias and quality assessment: Risk of bias will be appraised using the revised Cochrane Risk-of-Bias tool (RoB 2) for RCTs. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach will assess certainty of evidence.

Data synthesis and analysis: We will quantify depression severity using standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals. A random-effects model will be employed due to anticipated clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Subgroup analyses will explore moderator effects by intervention type, stroke chronicity (acute vs. chronic), and depression diagnostic criteria. Sensitivity analyses will examine the impact of excluding high-risk-of-bias studies. Funnel plots and Egger’s test will assess publication bias if ≥10 studies are available.

Results

A pilot search conducted in January 2025 yielded 1,247 unique citations after duplicate removal. Preliminary screening suggests approximately 45 full-text articles will warrant assessment for eligibility. Based on scoping, we anticipate 12 RCTs (*N* ≈ 1,203 participants) will meet inclusion criteria. Expected study characteristics include a mean sample size of 100 participants (range 32–214), publication years spanning 2014–2024, and intervention durations of 4–24 weeks. Aerobic training (*n* = 5), resistance training (*n* = 3), and tai chi/yoga (*n* = 4) represent the predominant modalities. Primary outcome measures include the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (*n* = 7) and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (*n* = 5). Approximately 25% of pilot-identified studies were conducted in East Asia, 33% in Europe, and 42% in North America. No serious adverse events directly attributable to exercise were reported in the pilot sample.

Discussion

This protocol outlines a robust methodology to synthesize the available evidence on exercise interventions for PSD. By incorporating diverse exercise modalities and stratifying analyses by stroke chronicity, this review will clarify whether specific intervention characteristics moderate antidepressant effects. The use of RoB 2 and GRADE will ensure transparent appraisal of evidence certainty. Limitations include the expected heterogeneity in intervention protocols, outcome measurement tools, and stroke severity across trials, which may preclude definitive conclusions for specific subgroups. Additionally, publication bias favoring positive results remains a concern in exercise psychology literature. Nonetheless, the anticipated yield of 12 RCTs provides adequate statistical power to detect a moderate effect size. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and will inform guideline panels, clinicians, and stroke survivors regarding the role of exercise in post-stroke mental health management.

Conclusion

This systematic review and meta-analysis protocol offers a transparent, replicable framework to evaluate exercise as a therapeutic strategy for post-stroke depression. The findings are expected to consolidate fragmented evidence and support the integration of structured physical activity into multidisciplinary stroke rehabilitation pathways.

title: Social problem-solving in Chinese baccalaureate nursing students
text:
Background: Social problem-solving (SPS) is a critical cognitive-behavioral competency that enables nursing students to navigate complex interpersonal dynamics and clinical challenges effectively. Despite its recognized importance in fostering professional competence and adaptive coping, empirical evidence concerning the current status and determinants of SPS among Chinese baccalaureate nursing students remains scarce.

Objective: This study aimed to examine the level of SPS and identify its associated sociodemographic and psychological factors among undergraduate nursing students in China.

Methods: A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,256 baccalaureate nursing students recruited through stratified random sampling from eight universities across four provinces between March and June 2024. Data were collected via validated online questionnaires, including a self-designed sociodemographic form, the Social Problem-Solving Inventory-Revised (SPSI-R), and the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC). Statistical analyses included independent t-tests, one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression.

Results: The mean total SPSI-R score was 89.64 ± 13.28, indicating a moderate overall level of SPS. Positive problem orientation and rational problem-solving subscales scored relatively high, whereas negative problem orientation and impulsivity/carelessness style exhibited lower mean scores with notable individual variability. Multiple regression analysis identified grade level, prior leadership experience, duration of clinical practice, and psychological resilience as significant independent predictors of SPS, collectively accounting for 34.8% of the variance (adjusted R² = 0.348, F = 18.642, p < 0.001). Additionally, students reporting stronger resilience and greater clinical exposure demonstrated significantly better SPS performance (p < 0.01).

Conclusion: Chinese baccalaureate nursing students demonstrate moderate social problem-solving ability with considerable room for enhancement. Nursing educators should incorporate resilience-building modules and structured problem-solving training early in undergraduate curricula to strengthen students' adaptive coping capabilities and readiness for professional clinical practice.
